records.name: Bonanza Falls / Greenwood Falls
records.title: Township upper-falls park verified; GIS point is outside mapped park
records.summary: Carp Lake Township explicitly lists Greenwoods (Bonanza Falls) as a public park with falls and publishes its map destination. The official map destination and regional upper-river view reference lie within a township-attributed parcel; Michigan's separate natural waterfall GIS #124 location lies outside it on a parcel attributed to a private LLC. The guide covers the short signed park approach to the upper falls only.
records.guidance: Use only the signed township park entrance and short established path from designated parking to the upper river view, then return. Do not drive to the GIS falls point, infer access to all downstream drops, or assume the seasonal park is open today.
records.locationNotes: Township Google Maps published destination 46.8176942,-89.5674561 (NOT verified lot); regional brochure upper-view reference 46.817719,-89.570023 (NOT surveyed viewpoint); state natural falls GIS #124 46.818863,-89.571458 on other attributed parcel. Route is signed, not surveyed or traced on the map.

records.reviewLimitations: Municipal park access is verified by the township's own Parks & Facilities directory, and a local guide describes a short signed lot-to-upper-falls path. Exact lot coordinates and trail geometry remain unverified; the published map has reference points only. Different parcels may apply farther downstream. The 2025 autumn closure minutes do not establish the 2026 park opening or closure date.
records.nextEvidence: For additional access, obtain mapped lawful public walking rights from the township upper viewing area toward any lower drops; verify current season entrance status. Do not extend the published signed upper-falls park route by inference.

records.name: Chicagon / Chicaugon Falls
records.title: DNR owns falls parcel; visitor right-of-way still unverified
records.summary: Michigan DNR's own land system identifies the natural Chicagon Falls point within a dedicated 47.8-acre Crystal Falls Management Unit parcel. The tourism approach via Raymer/Dave's Camp Road still passes private camps and may wash out. State ownership of the waterfall parcel does not create a legal visitor route, easement or parking on intervening land.
records.guidance: The waterfall's state parcel is verified, but do NOT navigate to the GIS point, cross private camps or assume Raymer/Dave's Camp Road is passable and public to its end. A signed, legal lot-to-view path needs verification before a visitor guide can be indexed.
records.locationNotes: Michigan GIS #12 at 46.134032,-88.452985 agrees broadly with other geographic catalogs around 46.1336,-88.4535; a separate tourism listing reports 46.1089,-88.4903, a materially different location. The latter must not be substituted as parking or falls position.
records.reviewLimitations: State land at the GIS falls is not the same as a documented continuous public right-of-way or permitted parking. Parcel polygon is administrative, not a survey. No same-day road status, current signage or ROW field inspection completed.
records.nextEvidence: Identify Raymer/Dave's Camp road title and public-access corridor, legal parking and continuous signed trail into DNR-managed falls parcel; source the access from DNR/township/road authority.

records.name: Gabbro / Baker's Falls
records.title: Gabbro/Baker's: City describes two approaches, land boundary pending
records.summary: The City of Bessemer identifies Gabbro/Baker's Falls as a sightseeing stop and describes a path near the bridge by Blackjack Ski Hill, plus an alternate upper route. Regional directions also mention a gas pipeline clearing. Neither source yet resolves a signed legally public lot-to-view trail or the crossing of adjacent parcels.
records.guidance: Use this research point to plan verification, not to drive to the waterfall GPS or follow an unsourced pipeline shortcut. A future guide requires a mapped legal parking approach and designated public viewing trail, with rough sections and seasonal conditions made explicit.
records.locationNotes: Michigan state GIS #38 marks the natural Black River falls; no separately certified visitor lot or full legal walking line has been established.
records.reviewLimitations: City scenic tourism recommendation is credible evidence of a visitor destination but does not itself certify all parcel access, maintained trail status or winter road clearance.
records.nextEvidence: Reconcile the City of Bessemer bridge/Blackjack Ski Hill route with public lot and legal footpath, and independently check upper-route land ownership.
